report.summary: Reviewed transport.py chunk 1: all docstring claims are kept; no defects found; one checkable claim about lock scope is verified.
risks: transport.py:71 | medium | The lock is created at sink construction time, not at publish time; if the same sink instance is used across multiple event loops, the lock will be bound to the first loop and may raise. | Verify whether the sink is ever shared across event loops; if not, this is benign.

handoff.purpose: Defines transport sink protocol and three sink implementations for runtime-shell records.

symbols.name: TransportSink
symbols.note: Protocol class; declares async publish method; no implementation.

symbols.name: InMemoryTransportSink
symbols.note: Stores records in a list; publish appends; deterministic for tests.

symbols.name: JsonlTransportSink
symbols.note: Appends JSON lines to a file; creates parent dirs; uses an asyncio lock for serialization.

symbols.name: CompositeTransportSink
symbols.note: Fans out to multiple sinks; does not catch or suppress errors.

claims.text: Persist or forward one lossless transport record.
claims.why: The protocol declares the method but does not implement persistence or forwarding; losslessness cannot be verified from the chunk.

claims.text: Small deterministic sink for tests and embedded consumers.
claims.why: The sink simply appends records to a list in publish order, which is deterministic and suitable for tests/embedded use.

claims.text: Append-only JSONL journal preserving every normalized input/output.
claims.why: Opens the file in append mode ('a') and writes each record as a JSON line; no truncation or overwrite occurs.

claims.text: Fan one record out to multiple sinks; failures remain visible.
claims.why: Iterates over sinks and awaits each publish without catching exceptions, so failures propagate to the caller.

observations.what: The asyncio.Lock is created in __init__, not per publish; if the sink is shared across event loops, the lock may be bound to the first loop and cause issues.
